checkedAgainst: brief.md section 2, lesson 2, and section 7 (the DOL sheet's four points, the PDF's 100% torque and two-line coil)

faults.finding: 'So its current falls by root 3 too' skips why: the winding's impedance is unchanged, so its current follows its voltage.
faults.fix: Add: the winding is the same, so its current falls in step with its voltage.

faults.finding: The overload's bimetal bending is given, but not why that stops the motor: the relay has no main contacts of its own, so it can only stop the motor by opening the coil circuit.
faults.fix: Add one sentence: the overload has no main contacts; it stops the motor only by opening the coil's circuit.

faults.finding: 'and burns out' / 'Too high burns it out': the source says too high a voltage could melt the coil, not that it always does.
'Starting, the motor draws 6 x 23.08 = 138 A to 8 x 23.08 = 185 A' drops the source's 'usually'.
'The overload cannot clear it' is stronger than the sources, which say fuses give short-circuit protection and are advised with the relay.
faults.fix: 'The overload is not made to clear it. Fuses or a breaker ahead of the starter do that.'

faults.finding: 'about 6 to 8 times rated' is one maker's making figure; another gives 5 to 7. Two near-identical ranges add nothing the starting-current row has not said.
faults.fix: Say it makes the full starting current and breaks only the running current; drop the multiple and its number entry.

faults.finding: 230 / 400 = 0.575 exactly; '0.58' could be read as a rounding slip.
None: the cause, the coil's path moving from Start to 7, is what lights; the worn-latch switch shows the side where the cause is missing and the effect fails.

None: both ask him to reason from the coil circuit (what has a path to the coil). Each wrong option is a named slip from brief section 4 (latch holds the contacts; DOL restarts after a cut) with its own hint.
Seven controls on a 340 px picture is a lot. The brief asks for all of them.
faults.fix: Keep, but tell the builder to put the five buttons in two rows under the drawing and the slider and fault switch below them; readouts in one row of three.

faults.fault: talks about the idea instead of teaching it
faults.finding: None found; the drawing is pointed at by part numbers, never by colour.
'Open that circuit anywhere, and the latch itself opens, so nothing can hold it in without Start' needs reading twice.
faults.fix: Say it in three short sentences: the magnet's supply does not pass through the door; the coil is fed through its own latching contact; once it lets go it has cut its own feed.

faults.where: whole lesson against brief section 2 and 7
faults.finding: All of lesson 2's screens are there with no recall opener: how it works with a still drawing, the live sheet, the power-cut check, characteristics, uses and limits with the at-sea line, star-delta on one screen with 138-185 A and 46-62 A, faults and tests, the latch fault check, Keep this. Item 7 is corrected without blame; the inrush line keeps both halves; rules of thumb taught as differing; fuses and no-volt protection added; the 100% torque slip corrected; the two-line coil covered. No sentence names a source.
The given rule (squared current minus 1) would trip at 105% after about 86 picture seconds, against the sourced 'no tripping at 1.05 x'.
faults.fix: Done in draft 1: threshold moved to 1.05 squared, 120% still fills in 20 s, 150% in about 6 s; examples file updated, cooling time added as an example value.

verdict: Rewrite as draft 2 with the fixes above.
